tools.name: tonight_sky
tools.description: Tonight's verdict for a Polish city: worth it, maybe or not, and why; the dark hours and the clearest stretch, MET Norway's cloud cover hour by hour, the moon's phase and whether it is up, a visible ISS pass, the chance of the aurora, the planets up and a meteor shower near its maximum. tools.name: iss_passes
tools.description: When the International Space Station can be seen with the naked eye over a Polish city in the next 10 days: each pass with its start, highest point and end (time, direction, height above the horizon) and brightness.

tools.name: aurora_forecast
tools.description: Whether the aurora can be seen in Poland tonight, from NOAA's Kp index: the level (none, only on a photo, to the naked eye low in the north, high in the sky) in the north, centre and south of Poland or in a given city, the Kp each needs, Kp now and the forecast for the next days.

tools.name: planets_tonight
tools.description: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn over a Polish city for the next seven nights: when each is at least 10° up in the dark, its highest point, brightness and the cloud cover then. Warsaw when no place is given.

tools.name: meteor_showers
tools.description: The twelve main meteor showers seen from Poland for the next twelve months: activity, maximum (Polish time), ZHR, the best hours on the night of the maximum and whether the moon gets in the way. With a shower (e.g. perseids, geminids, Leonidy) only that one, and for the six main ones its night in ea

tools.name: astronomy_picture
tools.description: Today's Astronomy Picture of the Day from NASA: its title, explanation (machine-translated into Polish with lang pl, when the translation is ready), credit and image address. Only today's picture.

tools.name: near_earth_objects
tools.description: The asteroids and comets passing Earth between two dates (seven days at most; today and the next six by default), from NASA's NeoWs: when each comes closest (Polish time), how far (km and lunar distances), how fast, how big, and whether NASA classes it as potentially hazardous, the closest first.
